summary.source: Wikipedia, Al Jazeera, IranStrikeMap, IranNewsWire, Flashpoint

succession.notes: Mojtaba survived subsequent airstrike. Trump called him 'lightweight'.

leaders.name: Ayatollah Ali Khamenei
leaders.details: Supreme Leader since 1989. Age 86. Killed in opening strike alongside daughter, son-in-law, and grandchild.

leaders.name: Mohammad Pakpour
leaders.details: Led IRGC ground forces for 16 years before appointment as IRGC commander-in-chief.
leaders.successor: Ahmad Vahidi (deputy, appointed by Khamenei 2 months prior)

leaders.name: Aziz Nasirzadeh
leaders.details: Iran's defense minister. Previously IRGC Air Force commander. Killed in opening strikes.

leaders.name: Ali Shamkhani
leaders.role: Secretary, Defense Council / Senior Adviser to Supreme Leader
leaders.details: Longtime security insider. Former head of Supreme National Security Council.

leaders.name: Mohammad Bagheri
leaders.role: Chief of Staff, Iranian Armed Forces
leaders.details: Top military coordination role. Confirmed dead by IDF.

leaders.name: Ali Larijani
leaders.details: Emerged as most influential figure coordinating national security after Khamenei's death. Killed in follow-up strike.

leaders.name: General Abdolrahim Mousavi
leaders.details: Coordinated between Iran's regular army and IRGC. One of most important operational commanders.

leaders.name: Esmail Khatib
leaders.details: Oversaw Iran's intelligence and internal security including counterintelligence operations.

leaders.name: Salah Asadi
leaders.details: Led intelligence for Iran's emergency command structure.

leaders.name: Mohammad Shirazi
leaders.role: Head of Military Affairs, Supreme Leader's Office
leaders.details: Military secretary to the Supreme Leader.

leaders.name: Jabal Amelian
leaders.details: Oversaw sensitive research projects linked to advanced military capabilities.

leaders.name: Baseri
leaders.details: Internal intelligence coordination. Less publicly known but tied to high-level security operations.

leaders.name: Hossein Taeb
leaders.killedBy: Israeli Air Force targeted strike on residence
leaders.details: Former IRGC intelligence chief. Killed in a later targeted strike on his personal residence.

leaders.name: Abolghasem Babaeian
leaders.role: Newly appointed military secretary to Supreme Leader
leaders.details: Appointed to replace Mohammad Shirazi. Killed shortly after appointment — demonstrating Israeli intelligence penetration.

leaders.name: Ismail Dehghan
leaders.details: Reportedly assassinated in Arak. IRGC Aerospace Force controls Iran's missile and drone programs.

leaders.name: Daoud Ali Zada
leaders.role: IRGC Quds Force Lebanon Corps Commander
leaders.details: Most senior Iranian commander in Lebanon. Managed Hezbollah operations against Israel.

leaders.name: Reza Khazaei
leaders.details: Chief of staff for IRGC operations in Lebanon. Killed alongside Daoud Ali Zada.

leaders.name: 4 unnamed Ministry of Intelligence officials
leaders.details: Names not publicly released. Reported by Iran International. Contributed to collapse of intelligence coordination.

leaders.name: Mojtaba Khamenei
leaders.role: New Supreme Leader (son of Ali Khamenei)
leaders.details: Appointed new Supreme Leader March 8 by Assembly of Experts. Survived subsequent Israeli airstrike March 10.

leaders.name: Masoud Pezeshkian
leaders.details: 9th President of Iran. Part of interim leadership council. Called Khamenei's death 'a wound to the nation'.

leaders.name: Ahmad Vahidi
leaders.details: Appointed deputy by Khamenei 2 months before war. Cited by IRGC Telegram channels as operational leader.

leaders.name: Gholam-Hossein Mohseni-Ejei
leaders.details: Part of interim leadership council. Former intelligence minister. Key role in maintaining judiciary continuity.
